raw_finding.practical_consequence: A fresh planner cannot produce trustworthy promotion and rollback steps for every directive consumer because several active writers, wrappers, target selectors, and validation surfaces are absent from the candidate evidence; it would have to rediscover or invent parts of the distribution path.
evidence: candidate-round-1.json#/requirement_statuses/CUR-002 declares complete topology but names only AGENTS, Claude hooks, Codex skill, installed skills, corpus, and evidence IDs P,A,C,N,Y,IS,IB; its evidence_index omits codex-projects.allowlist, inject-directives.sh, sync-corpus.sh, install-skills.sh, SETUP-codex.md, SETUP-claude.md, INSTALL.md, config.toml, and all four frozen validation-test files.

envelope-round-1.json#/required_current_evidence explicitly requires those omitted surfaces. Raw evidence shows concrete planner-relevant behavior: sync-corpus.sh:16-37 selects commit-triggered versus force-current sync and performs fail-open projection refresh; inject-directives.sh:2-14 defines the Claude injection consumer; install-skills.sh:3-5 runs validation before installation; generate_projections.py:67-73 and 133-153 derive targets from config and allowlist them; SETUP-codex.md:22-56 supplies preview/apply and verification observables; tests/test_generate_projections.py:94-194, tests/test_install_skills.py:22-130, and tests/test_sync_corpus.py:12-21 provide existing acceptance surfaces.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A planner cannot write a deterministic invocation-mistake scenario because the candidate simultaneously requires a corrected retry and a test expecting no correction, leaving the permitted action and acceptance oracle ambiguous.
evidence: candidate-round-1.json#/research_markdown states in the failure matrix "harmless pre-effect invocation→one retry" and in N11 "One no-effect corrected retry is allowed for unchanged invocation," but its adoption test list requires "typo no correction." The candidate does not define "no correction" as merely no durable remediation, so the stated expected behaviors conflict.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A fresh planner cannot assign one authoritative owner for the no-AI-attribution rule because the candidate both retains it in the universal contract and says to move it to an ungrounded publish sequence.
evidence: candidate-round-1.json#/research_markdown maps G12 with "D move publish sequence," includes "commits forbid AI attribution" in universal N7, and later states "publish owns attribution and commit/push gate." No publish sequence appears in the candidate evidence_index or the envelope required_current_evidence, and an rg --files check under the frozen skill roots found no publish-, yeet-, commit-, git-, or release-named skill surface. This violates the candidate's own FUT-004 research value "single_owner": true and leaves PO-FUT-004/PO-FUT-005 without a grounded relocation anchor.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A planner cannot preserve every justified current intent because several live mandates are replaced by proposed narrower behavior before their exact current triggers and actions are inventoried.
evidence: requirements.json CUR-001 requires the exact current authority, trigger, wording, and practical obligation of every G0-G24 rule, with mandatory actions, prohibitions, activation, and stop conditions.

working-agreement/DIRECTIVES.md:223-318 makes G17 create reusable scripts/skills, G18 check and guard registered sequences, G19 launch a separate remediation lane, G20 catalog every blocker before fixing, and G22 arm and re-arm a sleep-270 reporting timer.

candidate-round-1.json research_markdown instead records proposed behavior for these rows: G17 only authorized recurrence capture, G18 one activation with receipt reuse, G19 repair only when enabled, G20 only consequential reusable failures, and G22 moves the timer technique; it does not separately inventory the exact live mandates.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: Promotion could leave a governing surface stale or run without a checkable approval and validation boundary because the handoff does not name the complete topology or finite validation commands.
evidence: requirements.json CUR-002 requires every authoritative writer, generated consumer, installed copy, validation test, and external approval boundary to be named; FUT-009 requires finite validation commands, approval gates, and rollback conditions.

envelope-round-1.json required_current_evidence includes inject-directives.sh, sync-corpus.sh, install-skills.sh, both setup documents, INSTALL.md, codex-projects.allowlist, installed working-agreement and task-intake skills, .codex/config.toml, and four named validation test files.

candidate-round-1.json evidence_index omits those surfaces, while research_markdown only says 'validate', 'after approval', and 'run authority/scenario/safety tests' without naming exact commands, approval owners, or closure gates.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The same failure can still be routed differently by different executors because the proposed matrix names responses but not the evidence that objectively selects a class.
evidence: requirements.json FUT-003 requires objective classification evidence and exactly one permitted response for each failure class.

candidate-round-1.json research_markdown lists product, enabling-tool, out-of-scope infrastructure, invocation, anomaly, unavailable-evidence, and governance responses, but supplies no decision predicates or required observations that distinguish those classes; requirement_statuses nevertheless marks FUT-003 defined.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The scenario suite cannot serve as a deterministic proof oracle because most scenarios are labels rather than complete cases with both an expected action or stop and an explicit forbidden behavior.
evidence: requirements.json FUT-006 requires representative cases including remote operations, broken test tooling, broken governance tooling, and out-of-scope roots, each with expected and forbidden behavior.

candidate-round-1.json research_markdown compresses the suite into phrases such as 'feature frozen surfaces', 'research read/report only', and 'long run truthful cadence'; it does not provide a per-scenario input boundary, expected outcome, and forbidden outcome, while requirement_statuses reports 16 scenarios and defined=true.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A planner cannot prove that every obligation survives the redesign without crossing an exclusion because the candidate never explicitly records each requirement's conflict disposition and inclusion or exclusion boundary.
evidence: lenses-and-findings.md requires every atomic requirement to have a source, maturity, mechanism or conclusion, acceptance intent, conflict disposition, and explicit inclusion or exclusion.

requirements.json supplies source, maturity, acceptance intent, and scope IDs; candidate-round-1.json requirement_statuses supplies research values and evidence IDs, but neither the statuses nor the requirement-oriented conclusions explicitly disposition conflicts or map each requirement to the charter inclusions and exclusions.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The planner cannot prove which live obligations are preserved, changed, or retired because the purported current inventory already substitutes replacement behavior for several directives; the claim that no protected intent is lost is therefore unproven.
evidence: Tasks/directive-system-vnext/research-v2/requirements.json defines CUR-001 acceptance as an exact inventory of every current directive's activation and practical obligation and FUT-005 as a complete intent-preserving disposition map.

working-agreement/DIRECTIVES.md:223-285 makes G17 trigger on recurring/3+-step/external/build/deploy/auth sequences, G18 trigger broadly on operational turns, G19 mandate a separate remediation lane, and G20 mandate cataloging whenever any blocker appears.

Tasks/directive-system-vnext/research-v2/work/candidate-round-1.json research_markdown section G0-G24 instead records redesigned activations/actions: G17 'authorized recurrence capture', G18 'first operational boundary', G19 'repair only if enabled else stop', and G20 'active operational failure'. Its CUR-001 research value nevertheless declares complete=true and FUT-005 declares intent_loss=false.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A one-shot adoption plan could update the named surfaces yet miss the live post-commit coupling and its fail-open degradation, so canonical directives, AGENTS projections, and corpus state could diverge without the plan testing the actual writer path.
evidence: Tasks/directive-system-vnext/research-v2/requirements.json requires CUR-002 to name every authoritative writer, generated consumer, installed copy, validation test, and external approval boundary, and FUT-009 to define bounded synchronization and rollback across them.

working-agreement/sync-corpus.sh:16-37 shows that the normal post-commit wrapper conditionally invokes corpus synchronization and then refreshes trusted AGENTS projections, while failures are suppressed; force-current at lines 28-30 takes a different path and does not run projection refresh.

working-agreement/generate_projections.py:67-73 and 131-144 derive targets from Codex trusted-project configuration, intersect them with the explicit allowlist, and apply per-target skip/degradation behavior; tests/test_generate_projections.py:122-195 validates those selection and preservation boundaries.

Tasks/directive-system-vnext/research-v2/work/candidate-round-1.json CUR-002 reduces consumers to AGENTS, Claude hooks, Codex skill, installed skills, and corpus; its topology/adoption prose does not identify sync-corpus.sh as the dual writer trigger or bind the trusted-config/allowlist/skip behavior and corresponding tests into the claimed complete topology.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The planner receives two owners for the same commit-attribution rule, defeating the promised one-layer ownership model and making it unclear whether the canonical directive or publishing procedure is authoritative.
evidence: Tasks/directive-system-vnext/research-v2/requirements.json FUT-004 requires every retained obligation to exist at one correct authority layer without duplicated commands, while FUT-005 requires one exact disposition per current directive.

Tasks/directive-system-vnext/research-v2/work/candidate-round-1.json research_markdown maps G12 with disposition 'move publish sequence', proposed universal N7 independently commands that commits forbid AI attribution, and the downstream section states that publish owns attribution.
working-agreement/DIRECTIVES.md G12 defines the single current protected prohibition that this disposition must place unambiguously.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The planner would have to invent decision predicates and test oracles for failures, so the replacement cannot yet prove that each case yields one authorized action or one stop without recursive remediation or hidden scope growth.
evidence: Tasks/directive-system-vnext/research-v2/requirements.json FUT-003 requires objective classification evidence and exactly one permitted response for each failure class; FUT-006 requires the full representative suite with expected and forbidden behavior, explicitly including broken test tooling and broken governance tooling.

Tasks/directive-system-vnext/research-v2/work/candidate-round-1.json failure matrix leaves branches such as out-of-scope infrastructure 'diagnose/stop or amendment', anomalies 'authorized fix/stop', and unavailable evidence 'named route/stop' without predicates selecting one result.

The same candidate's scenarios section supplies terse expected outcomes but does not provide a per-scenario forbidden behavior matrix, does not explicitly instantiate the required broken-test-tooling case, and relies on a global non-recursion statement rather than deterministic acceptance oracles.
